objective: Derive exact clique-tree deficit accounting, classify positive deficit contributions at two and three, and construct infinite local-exchange obstructions with exact cp and a quadratic intact-core partition gap.

atomic_claims.text: For a clique tree rooted at an r-clique, delta=sum_i[a_i(r-|C_i|)+binom(a_i,2)], where a_i=|C_i minus its parent separator|.
Positive bag costs up to three have exactly the (a,h) types listed in C06 Section 3; at most delta bags and at most 2 delta introduced vertices have positive cost.
For all d>=2, k>=d+2, t>=k, the explicit nonsplit chordal G(k,t,d) has delta=d and exactly one outside edge for every maximum clique.
The explicit partition and signed edge-weight lower certificate both give cp(G(k,t,d))=k(t+2)-binom(k,2)-d-3.
For each maximum clique Q of G(k,t,d), cp_Q=k(t+1)-d-1, exceeding cp by binom(k,2)-k+2; benchmark scaling gives leading coefficients 2/9 and 1/6 respectively.

assumptions: Finite simple graphs; cp partitions edges exactly once.
The clique-tree structural characterization is the explicitly scoped input in C01 source S3.
The complete-graph matching decomposition and complete-split benchmark are the written constructions in C01.
risks: Natural-language candidate only; no mathematical code execution or verifier receipt.
The delta=2 and delta=3 table classifies positive bag contributions, not all clique-tree arrangements.
The local counterexamples do not negate the unrestricted split reduction; the family has explicit same-order split dominators.
cp_Q is a restricted partition minimum and must not be confused with cp.
The current-best literature coefficient and the full 1994 split paper remain unverified.

failed_route_proposal.blocker: Every nonsplit chordal graph with omega>=5, n-omega>=4, and delta=2 has a maximum clique whose complement contains at least two edges. This is a local-rule failure only; retain the admitted route and root as open. C06 also excludes asymptotic adequacy of always retaining an intact maximum-clique piece.
